---
title: "Week 7: Diffusion image generation"
description: "Build the forward process, the denoising loss, a time-aware U-Net, and the DDPM sampler; then diagnose and judge your generator, and find out how few sampling steps it needs."
---

Generate new images by learning to remove noise. Build the four parts of a small
diffusion model, test each one, and find out whether flawed samples come from
the sampler or from training. Then keep the trained network fixed and find out
how few sampling steps it needs.

The week has two notebooks, one for each session. Follow the
[setup instructions](https://github.com/HealthML/deep-learning-exercises/blob/main/exercises/week7/README.md) first.

## Session 1: build a diffusion model

Complete the exercises in [diffusion.ipynb](https://github.com/HealthML/deep-learning-exercises/blob/main/exercises/week7/diffusion.ipynb).

| Activity | Minutes |
|---|---:|
| 1. From predicting to generating | 5 |
| 2. The forward process: paper calculation, direct noising, schedules | 15 |
| 3. Learning to denoise: clean estimate and loss | 15 |
| 4. A U-Net that knows the noise level | 10 |
| 5. Train across all noise levels | 10 |
| 6. The reverse process: one DDPM step, generate, diagnose | 20 |
| 7. Judge the generator and individual exit ticket | 15 |
| 8. Extended exercise: fill in a hidden region | optional, 15 |

The core route takes **90 minutes**. Work in pairs and switch driver after
activity 3. Write a prediction before you run a comparison; the exit ticket is
individual. Pen-and-paper questions and response spaces are in the notebook.

The notebook assumes the Week 6 U-Net and the PyTorch training loop. Its notation
follows [Lesson 7: Diffusion Image Generation](https://healthml.github.io/deep-learning-book/chapters/07-diffusion/concepts.html).

## Session 2: how many denoising steps does an image need?

Complete the exercises in [diffusion_sampling.ipynb](https://github.com/HealthML/deep-learning-exercises/blob/main/exercises/week7/diffusion_sampling.ipynb).
The trained network stays fixed; you change only the sampler.

| Activity | Minutes |
|---|---:|
| Before you start: run the supplied parts, recall Session 1 while the network trains | 8 |
| 1. Try: a shortcut that skips timesteps, and the oracle's logbook | 15 |
| 2. Understand: the DDIM step, the jump plan, and the oracle test | 20 |
| 3. Experiment: 64, 16 and 4 network evaluations; find the breaking point | 20 |
| 4. Old noise or fresh noise? **or** 5. Extended exercise: ask for a disk on one side | 20 |
| 6. Individual exit ticket | 7 |

The route takes **90 minutes**. Activities 1 to 3 and the exit ticket are the
core; for the remaining 20 minutes each pair chooses activity 4 or activity 5.
Work in pairs and switch driver after activity 2. Write a prediction before you
run a comparison.

You do not need your notebook from Session 1: its parts are supplied,
completed. The session follows
[Lab 7: How Many Denoising Steps Do We Need?](https://healthml.github.io/deep-learning-book/chapters/07-diffusion/lab.html)
in the course book.
